case_name: A.A. Balasundaram vs A. Vijayakumari And Anr.
facts_of_case: The wife filed a petition alleging that the marriage between herself and the husband took place on 7-2-1987 at Rajahmundry in a temple as per Hindu rites. The trial Court found the marriage between the parties to be valid, but refused to grant maintenance on the ground that the husband has no source of income.

legal_principles.principle: Marriages performed in contravention of Clauses (i), (iv) and (v) of Section 5 of the Hindu Marriage Act are void.
legal_principles.held: As per Section 11 of the Hindu Marriage Act, the marriages performed in contravention of Clauses (i), (iv) and (v) of Section 5 of the said Act are void.

legal_principles.principle: Marriages that are voidable can be annulled by a decree of nullity on any of the grounds mentioned in Section 12 of the Hindu Marriage Act.
legal_principles.held: Under Section 12 of the Hindu Marriage Act, for contravention of any of the conditions enumerated therein, the marriages are voidable.

legal_principles.principle: The provisions of the Hindu Marriage Act do not render a marriage between a Hindu and a Christian void or voidable.
legal_principles.held: It is crucial to notice that neither Section 11 nor Section 12 of the said Act renders a marriage between a Hindu and a Christian void or voidable on the ground that the parties belong to two different religions.

outcome.final_order: The revision petition filed by the husband is directed against an order awarding maintenance of Rs. 150/- per month to the wife, whereas the criminal petition challenges the order confirming the finding of the Courts below that the marriage between the parties is a valid one.
